tagline: Across the old timber reserve, past the cradle of wilderness.
intro: Meeker is a ranching town in the wide valley of the White River. From there the byway heads east past Buford into the original White River Plateau Timberland Reserve, set aside in the late 19th century as the second unit of what became the National Forest system. It crosses Ripple Creek and Dunkley passes and comes down to Yampa, 82 miles on, through country still worked for mines, ranches and timber.

Around Trappers Lake, development of any kind was put off limits in 1920, the first Forest Service land set aside that way. It was recommended by Arthur Carhart, the man the Forest Service had hired to survey a road around the lake.

moments.title: Meeker
moments.text: Theodore Roosevelt stayed at the Hotel Meeker, opposite the courthouse, on hunting trips in 1901 and 1905, and the town holds the Meeker Classic Sheepdog trials every year.

moments.title: Trappers Lake
moments.text: At 9,633 feet, a lake a mile and a half long under the great semicircle of the Amphitheater, and the second-largest natural lake in Colorado.

moments.title: Yampa
moments.text: Named with the Northern Ute word for the Perideridia root, once an important food, in a town where the growing season averages about 80 days.

practical: Closed in winter on the west side at about mile 31 and on the east side at Dunkley Pass. The roads are muddy when wet.

sources.label: Colorado Department of Transportation, Flat Tops Trail
